marketPulse: Hot CPI 3.8% + Iran 'Life Support' Reversal — Semis Buckle Hard, Then Recover. S&P Ekes Above 7,400 for First Time.
marketPulseSubtext: S&P 500 +0.19% to 7,412.84 (first close above 7,400 — new record), Nasdaq +0.10% to 26,274.13 (new record), Dow +0.19% to 49,704.47, Russell 2000 TBD — indexes clawed back from 2%+ intraday declines to close marginally green. April CPI 3.8% YoY (highest in 3 years), core 2.8% — energy +18%, gasoline +28%. Trump called Iran truce 'life support,' 'unbelievably weak.' QCOM -13.3% (worst semi day since 2020), INTC -8%, SOX -5% intraday but recovered. VIX +6.9% to 18.38. WTI above $101 at highs, closed near $101-103 range. Copper hit new record close $6.46. Cerebras priced $135/share (raised from $125, 20x oversubscribed) — IPO Thursday. Trump-Xi meeting this week in China.
topDriver: CPI 3.8% (3-year high) + Iran 'life support' = the stagflation regime is now quantified. Semis sold off hard on combined inflation and geopolitical risk, then partly recovered on AI conviction holding.
narrativeSummary: May 12 was the day the market got the bill for the Iran war. April CPI came in at 3.8% YoY — the highest since May 2023 and above the 3.7% consensus — with energy prices up 18%, gasoline up 28%, and fuel oil up 54%. Core CPI at 2.8% was also above the 2.7% estimate, showing that Iran's energy shock is bleeding into broader prices. RSM chief economist Joseph Brusuelas warned the headline rate is heading toward 4% later this year. Before the open, oil had already risen 3% above $100 on CNN's report that Trump was more seriously thinking of restarting combat operations in Iran. Then the CPI hit and Trump confirmed the ceasefire is on 'life support' — 'unbelievably weak' were his words — after rejecting Iran's counteroffer as 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE.' The morning was brutal: QCOM -13.3% (its worst day since 2020), INTC -8%, SOX -5%, Nasdaq down over 2% at session lows. But the market found its footing. By the close, AI conviction reasserted itself — investors continued pouring money into AI-linked technology names — and all three major indexes managed marginal gains. The S&P 500 closed at 7,412.84, its first close above 7,400. The session's secondary theme was copper reaching a new record close of $6.4605 — up 13% in 2026 — driven by AI data centre construction demand. Cerebras Systems priced its IPO at $135/share (raised from $125), making it 20x oversubscribed and the largest pure-play AI hardware IPO of the year, pricing ahead of Thursday's Nasdaq debut. Trump's China visit this week adds a trade-policy dimension to the already-complex macro environment.
macroStressSubtext: CPI 3.8% — highest in 3 years — plus Iran ceasefire 'life support' drives MSI to 76. Energy inflation now structurally embedded in core.
rateCurveRead: The curve bear-steepened sharply on May 12 as CPI 3.8% — highest in three years — forced a repricing of the inflation trajectory. The 10Y rose 6bps to 4.42% from 4.36% (May 7), and the 30Y returned to 4.98%, back near its recent 5.02% high. The 2Y rose 8bps to 3.95%, the biggest single-day 2Y move of the month, as markets reduced near-term cut expectations — Schwab's Cooper Howard noted core CPI 2.8% 'weakens the case for Fed rate cuts in the near-term.' The 2/10 spread compressed slightly to +47bps. The key signal: the 5Y rose 8bps to 4.07%, confirming that inflation expectations are being repriced across the mid-curve, not just the long end. The energy inflation is no longer transient-adjacent — the market is pricing it as a sustained structural shift. Warsh's June 17 inaugural meeting now faces a 3.8% CPI backdrop. Source: Federal Reserve H.15, May 12, 2026 official release.

drivers.name: CPI 3.8% — Highest in 3 Years. Energy +18%, Gasoline +28%, Fuel Oil +54%. Core 2.8% Beats.
drivers.source: BLS April 2026 CPI release, Schwab Market Update, RSM, 24/7 Wall St.
drivers.detail: April CPI 3.8% YoY — the highest since May 2023, above the 3.7% consensus — confirmed that the Iran war's energy shock is fully embedded in the inflation basket. Energy +18% YoY, gasoline +28%, fuel oil +54%. Monthly CPI +0.6% met consensus; annual was the shock. Core CPI 2.8% YoY exceeded the 2.7% estimate and 0.4% MoM — the Iran energy shock is bleeding into broader prices through transportation and logistics costs. RSM chief economist Brusuelas: 'The American economy has entered a new chapter where inflation appears to have stepped up.' He predicts headline reaching 4% later this year. Schwab's Cooper Howard: core 2.8% 'weakens the case for Fed rate cuts in the near-term.' fedTransitionRisk raised to 78 — Warsh now inherits the worst inflation backdrop since 2023 at his June 17 debut. realWageYoY deteriorated to -1.1% (wages losing purchasing power in real terms).

drivers.name: Iran Ceasefire 'On Life Support' — Trump Rejects Counteroffer, Considers Combat Restart
drivers.detail: Trump called the ceasefire 'unbelievably weak, on life support' in an Oval Office statement Monday after rejecting Iran's counteroffer as 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE.' Iran had demanded sanctions relief, war reparations, and greater control over the Strait of Hormuz — terms the US flatly rejected. CNN reported Trump is more seriously thinking of restarting combat operations. Hormuz commercial traffic at a fraction of capacity. The 14-point US framework is stalled; no diplomatic breakthrough visible. WTI back above $101, Brent at $107-108 — the peace deal pricing from May 6-7 has been fully reversed. hormuzclosurePct downgraded back to 6% as diplomatic progress stalls.

drivers.name: Cerebras IPO Priced at $135 — 20x Oversubscribed. Wafer-Scale AI Hardware Conviction Holds.
drivers.linked: CBRS, AI hardware, SOXX, Nvidia May 20
drivers.detail: Cerebras Systems priced its Nasdaq IPO at $135/share, raised from the $125-135 range (previously $115-125) due to more than 20x oversubscription. Raising $3.5-3.8B. Fully diluted valuation $26-27B. The company's Wafer-Scale Engine (WSE-3) is 57x larger than the largest GPU die — fundamentally different architecture from Nvidia. Revenue $510M in 2025 (+76% YoY) with a 47% net margin. 750MW compute deal with OpenAI. Morgan Stanley, Citigroup, Barclays, UBS leading. The fact that this priced $10/share above the top of the original range on a day when QCOM fell 13% is the clearest possible signal that institutional AI hardware conviction is structural, not momentum-driven.

drivers.name: Copper Record Close — AI Data Centre Construction Driving Structural Commodity Demand
drivers.linked: XLB, copper, Materials sector, AI infrastructure
drivers.detail: Copper closed at a new record of $6.4605, up 13% in 2026, hitting $6.509 intraday. Schwab: 'drawing support from construction demand associated with the data centre buildout.' AI data centres require enormous quantities of copper for power distribution, cooling systems, and networking. This is the same physical AI infrastructure trade that drove Caterpillar +10% and Corning's $500M Nvidia deal — now showing up in industrial commodities. Silver also gained 3% intraday. Materials +1.4% the second-best S&P sector.

drivers.name: Trump-Xi Beijing Meeting This Week — AI, Trade, Rare Earths, Technology Access
drivers.linked: China, rare earths, AI supply chain, trade policy
drivers.detail: Trump visiting China for talks with President Xi Jinping this week. Schwab's Michelle Gibley: meeting is 'more to keep the peace on the trade war, although there may be some purchase agreements and discussions about access to technology and rare earths.' China's CPI is rising due to Iran oil — welcomed as deflation relief after years of deflationary pressure. Any agreement on rare earths access would directly benefit the AI semiconductor supply chain. The timing — simultaneous with a 3.8% US CPI print and Iran ceasefire stress — makes the diplomatic context more complex.

risks.title: CPI heading to 4% — Iran energy shock embedding in core, real wages falling at -1.1%
risks.desc: RSM chief economist Brusuelas explicitly forecast CPI reaching 4% later this year if the Iran war continues. Core CPI at 2.8% confirms the shock is no longer transient-adjacent — it's in services and transportation. Real wage growth is now -1.1% YoY, meaning workers are losing purchasing power in real terms. Median American families face 'very challenging' conditions into H2 2026. The political pressure on Trump to resolve Iran is building, but his 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE' response to Iran's counteroffer suggests resolution is not imminent.

risks.title: Warsh June 17 debut with 3.8% CPI — fedTransitionRisk 78, hike probability rising
risks.desc: Warsh inherits the worst inflation backdrop since 2023 at his first FOMC meeting June 17. With CPI at 3.8% and core at 2.8%, the case for a rate hold is obvious — but the case for a hike is now being discussed openly. CME FedWatch hike probability has risen from 9.1% last week. The combination of Warsh's hawkish-leaning history and a 3.8% CPI makes the June 17 statement the most consequential Fed communication in two years. fedTransitionRisk raised to 78.

risks.title: Nvidia May 20 — Cerebras and QCOM's 13% drop set up a bifurcated expectation
risks.desc: Cerebras pricing 20x oversubscribed shows AI hardware conviction is intact — the bar for Nvidia is therefore very high. But QCOM's -13.3% on no specific news shows how quickly the market can reprice semi exposure on macro shock. Nvidia at 35x+ forward needs data center > $45B and Q2 guide > $50B to justify the multiple. Michael Burry reportedly doubled his short positions in Nvidia and Palantir — a contrarian signal worth noting even if not consensus.

risks.title: Shiller CAPE ratio at 40 — historically elevated, 'correction followed every time above 30'
risks.desc: FactSet data shows the Shiller CAPE ratio at approximately 40 — more than double the historical median of 17. Every previous extended period above 30 has eventually led to a major correction. The S&P 500 is now above 7,400 with CPI at 3.8% and Iran unresolved. This is not a crash prediction — but the valuation multiple provides very little cushion for earnings disappointment or inflation surprise.

risks.title: Semiconductor breadth collapse — QCOM -13.3%, INTC -8%, SOX -5% intraday on no new earnings
risks.desc: QCOM's worst day since 2020 was not driven by an earnings miss — it was macro. The combined impact of CPI 3.8% (reducing device upgrade cycle expectations), Iran risk (global smartphone market disruption), and a crowded semi sector after the parabolic run produced an outsized unwind. If Nvidia May 20 disappoints, this pattern — where macro shock + crowded trade = violent derating — repeats at a much larger scale.

Nvidia at 35x+ forward needs a massive blowout — data center >$45B, Q2 guide >$50B — to sustain the multiple into a 3.8% CPI environment. Burry's doubled short in NVDA and PLTR is not consensus but is worth noting. Reduce Nvidia position by 20-30% ahead of May 20 and reload if the print is the blowout the trade requires.
